reference.title: WHO 5th thymic epithelial tumours & AJCC 9th (2025) staging
reference.intro: AJCC 9th (2025) splits pT1 by tumour size (pT1a <= 50 mm vs pT1b > 50 mm) and moves direct invasion of lung and phrenic nerve into pT2 alongside pericardium. Report mixed thymomas in 10% increments.
reference.note: Photomicrographs are from Wikimedia Commons under open Creative Commons licences. ExpertPath pages open with your own ExpertPath login; the app holds none of their images.

groups.heading: WHO 5th subtypes, IHC & AJCC 9th revisions
points: Thymoma A (bland spindle/oval cells, TdT-poor) vs AB (A + lymphocyte-rich B-like areas) vs B1 (resembles normal thymus with medullary islands) vs B2 (polygonal epithelioid clusters in dense TdT+ T-cell background) vs B3 (sheets of mildly atypical polygonal cells, sparse TdT+ cells).
Thymic squamous cell carcinoma is typically CD5+, CD117 (KIT)+, GLUT1+, PAX8+ (polyclonal) and lacks TdT+ immature thymocytes.

AJCC 9th pT: pT1a <= 5 cm, pT1b > 5 cm (thymus/mediastinal fat/mediastinal pleura); pT2 = pericardium, lung, or phrenic nerve; pT3 = brachiocephalic vein, SVC, chest wall, or extrapericardial pulmonary vessels; pT4 = aorta, arch vessels, intrapericardial pulmonary vessels, myocardium, trachea, or oesophagus.

images.caption: Type B1 thymoma: lymphocyte-rich organoid lobules closely recapitulating normal thymic cortex with paler medullary islands (H&E).
Type B2 thymoma (intermediate magnification): lobules of polygonal epithelial cells amidst dense immature T lymphocytes (H&E).
Thymic carcinoma: infiltrating nests of overtly malignant epithelial cells within a desmoplastic stroma lacking immature thymocytes (H&E).
